tasks.short: Field manager and employee questions, apply contracts and CAO to cases, help resolve work problems.

steps.what: Receive question or issue by mail, Teams, phone or on the floor

loop.input: free-text question from Teams or mail
loop.output: category (general policy, contract, personal case, conflict) plus urgency
loop.check: category must be in a fixed list; personal and conflict categories always route to the HRBP of that site
loop.stop: one pass; low confidence or no category goes to the HRBP queue unclassified
loop.why_not_simpler: questions arrive as free text in Dutch and English; a form alone is ignored by shift managers

steps.what: Look up contract, CAO article, absence and history in AFAS and SharePoint
Interpret contract and CAO for this case and decide HR position

loop.input: case brief plus retrieved CAO and contract clauses
loop.output: draft reading of the relevant clauses with citations
loop.check: every claim must cite a clause id that exists in the indexed CAO or contract template; uncited text is dropped
loop.stop: one draft; if no clause found it says so and the HRBP works from scratch
loop.why_not_simpler: matching a messy situation to clause text needs reading free text

steps.what: Talk with manager and employee to resolve the problem
Record outcome, send confirmation letter, request contract change in AFAS

tasks.design: A Teams front door (Copilot Studio or a small app on the M365 tenant) takes questions, classifies them with one bounded model call and answers general policy from the indexed SharePoint and CAO content; personal and conflict cases open a case in a SharePoint list with an auto-built case brief from the AFAS API. The HRBP gets a draft clause reading with citations, does the conversation, and a Power Automate flow turns the agreed outcome into a template letter and an AFAS change request for HR admin.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrive as unstructured talk and mail, and pulling contract, absence and CAO context took manual clicks in three places.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit connectors and cheap retrieval over owned documents make a case brief and a cited clause draft a few days of build.
tasks.still_hard: Trust from shift workers and managers who expect a person, and cases where the facts are disputed; the model must never decide a personal case.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the room between a site manager and a worker, choosing what to concede, and being trusted by both sides.

ambition.what: Night and weekend shift workers in the warehouses get answers to contract and roster questions in their own shift instead of waiting for an office-hours HRBP.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP spends less time looking things up and more time on the 20-30 real conflicts per month per site; they decide which case categories the desk may answer alone.

reach.learn: Which change requests arrive incomplete and what fields the template must force.
Which CAO allowance questions keep coming back so the desk can answer them from payroll rules.

evidence.claim: IBM's Ask HR handles over 11 million interactions a year, with HRBPs as first human support for escalated complex cases.
Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent serves 1,200 of 3,600 staff monthly and opens tickets for what it cannot answer.
Employee-facing bots must disclose they are AI.
Works council consent is needed before AI processes personnel data.
AFAS Profit exposes data through GetConnectors and UpdateConnectors usable for a case brief.

assumptions: The CAO texts and contract templates are current in SharePoint.
Most questions from managers repeat across the three sites.
unknowns: Share of questions that are personal cases versus general policy.
Whether the OR will consent to case logging of questions about named employees.
Whether IT allows an AFAS API user with read access to contracts and absence.
research_questions: Of last month's 100 HRBP mails and Teams threads, how many could be answered from policy text alone?
Does the case brief cut lookup time by more than half in a two-week shadow test?
Do shift workers actually use a Teams bot, or do they need a phone or kiosk channel?

tasks.short: Explain HR policies, CAO rules, procedures and Dutch law to managers and employees.

steps.what: Receive policy question from manager or employee
Find the right policy page, CAO article or law text

loop.input: question plus indexed policies, both CAOs and selected law texts
loop.output: ranked list of clauses with document version
loop.check: only documents from the approved SharePoint library and wetten.overheid.nl are indexed
loop.stop: top five clauses; none above threshold means escalate
loop.why_not_simpler: keyword search fails on everyday wording like 'snipperdag' versus 'verlof'

steps.what: Write explanation in plain Dutch or English

loop.output: short answer with clause citations and an AI disclosure line
loop.check: every sentence must map to a cited clause; questions naming a person, absence, dismissal or pay dispute are never answered and go to the HRBP
loop.stop: one answer; if the check fails, a ticket to the HRBP with the draft attached
loop.why_not_simpler: answers must be phrased for the asker's situation, which a static FAQ cannot do

steps.what: Handle follow-ups, edge cases and personal situations
Fix unclear or missing policy text

tasks.design: An answer desk in Teams built on the M365 tenant retrieves from one approved SharePoint library (policies, both CAOs, poortwachter procedure) and answers general questions with citations and an AI disclosure; anything personal becomes a ticket for the site HRBP. A weekly report of unanswered and escalated questions feeds policy fixes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier bots needed hand-built intent trees and failed on Dutch everyday wording and CAO detail.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval with a model that cites clauses, on content HR already owns, is now standard in M365 and similar tools.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the source library current and versioned, and a wrong answer on law (ontslag, verzuim) has legal cost; the escalation line must be strict.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a 'general' question is really about one person, and explaining a hard rule so it is accepted.

ambition.what: Every new team leader gets a policy answer within minutes for every question, instead of saving them up for the monthly HRBP meeting.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP stops answering the same leave and overtime questions and owns the escalated cases and the quality of the policy library.

reach.learn: The top 20 questions new leaders ask, to build them into onboarding.
Which policies generate most confusion, measured, not guessed.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina runs an HR policy agent with ticket fallback, CSAT 4.1.
IBM Ask HR saved about 40% with HRBPs as second line.
Average time saved by HR staff using chatbots was about 3%.
AI disclosure is required for systems interacting with people.

assumptions: Policies live in one SharePoint library that HR controls.
Questions in Dutch and English, some Polish speakers among warehouse staff.
unknowns: How many policy questions per week reach the three HRBPs today.
Whether the policies and CAO summaries are up to date.
research_questions: In a two-week test on 200 real past questions, what share does the desk answer correctly with citations?
How often does a 'general' question turn out to be personal, and does the filter catch it?
Do managers keep using the desk after week four?

tasks.short: Match staff to roles, shifts and sites: redeployment, internal moves, peak-season staffing.

steps.what: Collect staffing needs and vacancies from site managers
Gather available staff, contract hours, valid certificates and absence
Shortlist matches, weigh fit, preferences and reintegration limits
Agree moves with managers and employees
Process change in AFAS, tell payroll and agency

tasks.design: Replace the site Excel sheets with a Power Apps request form and a nightly job on the existing Power BI extract that joins AFAS contracts and absence, Studytube certificates and agency headcount into a filterable availability view with hard-rule filters (valid forklift or VCA, contract hours, CAO working-time limits). The HRBP picks matches by hand; a Power Automate flow sends approved moves to HR admin and the agency order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificate, contract and absence data sit in three systems and the agency portals, so matching ran on memory and Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the join, filters and form a short build on data that already reaches Power BI nightly.
tasks.still_hard: No ranking or scoring of people: allocating tasks on traits or behaviour is high-risk under Annex III 4(b) from December 2027 and needs OR consent; agency portal data may only come as files.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who works well together, who is fragile after absence, and negotiating a move a person accepts.

ambition.what: Weekly redeployment review across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo before ordering flex workers, instead of each site ordering agency staff alone.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP reviews a cross-site availability view weekly and decides internal moves before agency orders go out.

reach.learn: How to add Studytube certificates and agency headcount to the model.
How internal moves change agency spend per site.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers structure and staffing without asking HR.
AI allocating tasks on behaviour or traits is high-risk from 2 December 2027.
OR consent is needed for systems that can observe behaviour or performance.

assumptions: Studytube has an export or API for certificate expiry dates.
Reintegration limits are recorded in AFAS absence cases.
unknowns: How the three agency portals export orders and headcount.
How often internal moves happen per month per site.
Whether sites will give up their own staffing sheets.
research_questions: In the last peak season, how many agency orders could have been filled by idle certified staff on another site?
Can Studytube certificate data be joined to AFAS employee ids reliably?
Will the OR accept a view showing absence status next to availability?

tasks.short: Advise management on recruiting and retention programmes using hiring and turnover data.

steps.what: Pull time to hire, acceptance, 90-day retention and turnover figures
Read exit interviews, onboarding feedback and manager remarks

loop.output: theme per comment from a fixed list (pay, shifts, manager, travel, workload, other) with quote
loop.check: themes from the fixed list only; HRBP samples 10% and corrects
loop.stop: one pass per comment; unclear goes to 'other' for manual read
loop.why_not_simpler: reasons are free text; counting keywords misses most of them

steps.what: Draft advice note with options, cost and expected effect

loop.input: figures, themes and a note template
loop.output: first draft of the advice note
loop.check: every number must come from the dashboard dataset; HRBP edits options and recommendation
loop.stop: one draft; HRBP rewrites as needed
loop.why_not_simpler: the structure is fixed but the argument changes per site and season

steps.what: Discuss with management and agree the programme
Track programme effect in the following months

tasks.design: Extend the nightly Power BI model with Recruitee pipeline data so the North Star (filled roles still productive at day 90) and its inputs show per site and job family; a bounded model step tags pseudonymised exit and onboarding comments into fixed themes. A Word template plus one draft step produces the advice note, which the HRBP rewrites and presents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitee and AFAS data were never joined, so each advice note started with a manual Excel exercise and exit comments went unread.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitee's API and the existing AFAS extract can be joined with little code; theme tagging of short comments is cheap and checkable.
tasks.still_hard: Proving cause: a retention dip may be the season or one manager; the advice still rests on HRBP judgement and site knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a site director that their own team leader is the retention problem, and getting a programme funded.

ambition.what: A quarterly retention review per site with each site director, instead of an ad hoc note when turnover is already high.

tasks.altitude: The HRBP spends advice time on options and persuasion, not on building figures, and brings a site-level retention agenda to each quarterly review.

reach.learn: Which stages lose candidates per job family and site.
How to define 90-day productive retention in AFAS data.

evidence.claim: Workday HRBPs built narrow agents that cut prep time by up to 75% for half of users.
Satisfaction and comment reports suit dashboards plus a model step over comments.
Recruitee offers an API for candidates and pipeline stages.

assumptions: Exit interviews are written down somewhere searchable.
Recruitee candidate ids can be linked to AFAS employee ids at hire.
unknowns: Whether exit and onboarding feedback is stored consistently across sites.
How often management asks for retention or recruiting advice.
Retention of exit comments under the AVG retention policy.
research_questions: Can 90-day retention per site be computed from current AFAS and Recruitee data without manual fixes?
Do HRBPs agree with model themes on 90% of a 100-comment sample?
Did any past programme change 90-day retention measurably?

role.altitude: The HRBP moves from answering and looking things up to second-line case handling and site advice: the answer desk and case briefs take routine questions, and the three HRBPs spend their weeks on conflicts, redeployment decisions and quarterly retention reviews with site directors.
reach: Recruiter: pipeline drop-off per job family feeds retention advice
HR admin: complete change requests from case outcomes
People analytics: shared AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data model
L&D: new team leader questions shape onboarding
skills_to_grow: Owning and versioning a policy content library
Reading dashboards and challenging the figures
Writing escalation rules for an answer desk
EU AI Act and WOR consent basics for HR tools
role.ambitious_version: HRBPs organised in pods per value stream (hire to productive, absence to return) across the three sites, with a Teams answer desk as front door for all 1,200 staff including night shifts, and a weekly cross-site staffing and retention review that cuts agency orders and lifts 90-day retention.
